subject: Ability registry
notes: Every line of effect text is transcribed verbatim from the in-game Active Abilities panel.
`cooldown` and `active_time` come from the in-game panel; neither published source carries them.
`note` holds the italic line the game prints under the effect - either that the ability works passively once equipped, or that it does not take up a common slot in the Active Abilities panel.
`no_common_slot` marks an ability that does not consume one of the tree's ability slots.
Activation charge and health costs to use an ability come from the in-game Cost line, cross-checked against the Fextralife ability table.
The source labels the fourth row of four-level abilities 'Lv. 3'; levels here are numbered by position.
Abilities have no prerequisites in either source - they are learned independently of the perk graph.
Gates: manual, corruption <n>, road shrine, vrakhir blood (a Phial of Vrakhir Blood), or none.
Some levels cost skill points but no time segments, so `time_segments` can be 0.
A level whose cost the game hides is one the capture's save had already bought; those costs are kept from the published tables.

`kind` is active or passive, decided by use_cost: anything that pays an activation charge or health is active. Passive abilities still take an ability slot - they work once equipped in the Active Ability panel.
`story_granted` marks an ability whose first level the story hands you: it costs no skill points and no time segments to learn. Upgrades past level 1 are paid for normally.

`text_source` records where each level row's text came from: `game` (read from the in-game panel), `game8` (still the Game8 table, never re-read from the game), or `placeholder` (a padlocked story node that prints no effect line).

`scales` lists a level row's absolute damage figures and `effect_template` is the row with each of them replaced by a positional slot, so the text can be restated at another character level without re-parsing it. See `scaling`.

scaling.note: Every figure in `scales` is what the in-game panel shows a character at `anchor_level`. Damage scales with the character, so figures read at different levels are not comparable - splice two and an upgrade reads as a downgrade. `ratio` is a tree's figure at `anchor_level` divided by the same figure at `low_anchor_level`, measured on rows captured at both. To restate a figure at level L: multiply by 1 + (1/ratio - 1) * (anchor_level - L) / (anchor_level - low_anchor_level). That is exact at both anchors and interpolates between them; outside 9-20 it is extrapolation.
scaling.model_note: `linear` is a straight line between the two anchors, not compounding growth. Both models fit the anchors exactly and diverge by up to 6.7% midway between them, so the data cannot yet separate them - a capture at a third known level would. Linear is preferred because it places the first, unknown-level capture at level 11.9-12.3 in all three trees, against 12.7-13.2 and a wider spread for geometric. Per-level growth under this model is `per_level_of_low_anchor` of the level 9 figure, each level: about 9.1% for Swordmastery and 10.1-10.2% for the other two.
scaling.scaled_rows: Rows marked figure_source: scaled were not read at anchor_level; figure_note records the arithmetic. Rows marked read were.
scaling.first_capture: The registry's original capture was at no single level: its three trees imply levels 11.9, 12.0 and 12.3, so it straddled a level-up. That is why its figures could not be reconciled and why level 20 is the anchor.
scaling.observations_note: Figures read from a panel at a character level other than `anchor_level`, keyed by that level then by ability then by ability level. verify_perks.py restates each `scales` entry at that level through the model and fails if it does not come back to what the panel showed, so the model cannot drift from its evidence. null marks a figure the capture did not show.
